request.spec:
Show on each person their statements, one line per statement still standing (a cancelled one is
gone), oldest first, as <statement date> <due-total>. The statements a merge or a transfer brings
over show among them, by date.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their statements, one line per statement still standing (a cancelled one is
gone), oldest first, as <statement date> <due-total>. The statements a merge or a transfer brings
over show among them, by date.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the statement lines to each person's row. Three of the four tests in `bin/e2e` pass. "statement lines scenario 2" fails at a check on a claim's due figure, which my change doesn't touch.

**The change**
- **Server** (`PersonController.java`): the person data the screen loads now includes `statementLines`, one `<date> <due-total>` line per statement on record. They're sorted oldest first by date; statements with the same date stay in the order they were taken. A due-total that was n/a shows as `n/a`, the same as "last stated".
- **No database change was needed.** Statements are already stored per person. Cancelling one deletes it, so it disappears from the list. A merge or transfer already copies the other person's statements over, and sorting by date puts them in place among the person's own.
- **Front end:** `people.ts` (model) and `features/people/people.ts` (screen) gain a "Statement lines" column, with each line under `data-testid="person-statement-line-line"`. No existing ids changed.

**The scenario 2 failure** (`e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts:800`): a draft claim is expected to show a due of `1.29` while the sheet is viewed as of 2026-03-20, but it shows `n/a`. Every statement-line check before that point passes, including the one at line 790; the test stops at line 800, so the three statement-line checks after it (lines 852, 1069, 1131) never ran.

I think the cause is the real-world date, though I didn't confirm it from stored data:
1. The claim gets its rate from the parent sheet (`<sheet>-p`). That sheet was never given a "today" of its own, so it took the server's real date, 2026-11-13.
2. Rate changes are stamped with the sheet's today when they're made, so the parent's rates were all recorded on 2026-11-13.
3. Viewed as of 2026-03-20, the parent had no rates yet, so the claim has no rate and shows n/a.

This would only have passed if the test ran before 2026-03-20. Fixing it would mean changing how a parent sheet's rates are dated in the as-of view. That's outside this request, so I left it alone; tell me if you want me to take it on.
